text:
ashwin: FYI ran a focused perf pass on INT8/FP8 KV paths after the canary rollout, saw a 18% p50 token latency increase for cold-prefixes. attaching quick logs and flame output below.

marie: ack, can you paste the flame and the exact commit?

ashwin: commit c3f9b2d — the prefetch + kernel-handoff change. flame: `decode_loop -> kv.read_prefetch -> kernel_select(INT8_vs_FP8) -> kernel_dispatch` shows a new spin in kernel_select when kv page miss rate > 0.02.

sam: how does this correlate with KV occupancy? memory footprint change?

ashwin: footprint down ~12% on INT8 encoders for cached pages, but cold-path latency up. numbers: avg token p50 8.4ms -> 9.9ms, p99 42ms -> 51ms. KV memory: 6.8GB -> 6.0GB for the shard.

evelyn: interesting — sounds like we're trading memory for a scheduling jitter somewhere. any batching changes?

ashwin: yes, batching heuristics now allow earlier make-up batches when prefetch in flight. when prefetch hits a page miss we go into a fallback kernel that probes INT8 calibration table and sometimes falls back to slower FP8 code path with extra dequant ops.

marie: can you paste the kernel selection snippet?

ashwin: ```
// simplified
if (kv_hit) { use_int8_kernel(); } else { // warmup
  if (prefetch_inflight && calib_score < 0.7) use_fp8_slowpath();
  else use_int8_probe();
}
```

sam: is calib_score the online quantization confidence? where does it come from?

ashwin: it's from the per-shard calibration stats we compute during model load + first few decodes. it's noisy on mixed traffic (short vs long prefixes).

perf-bot: CI perf check #485: branch c3f9b2d triggered +17% p50 on kv-heavy replay workload. Full histograms: https://perf.redwood/ci/485 (short link). :warning:

marie: OK looks like two issues: (1) our prefetch -> kernel handoff adds a branching penalty when a miss occurs, (2) the FP8 slowpath has extra dequant/quant roundtrips. both amplify at small batch sizes.

evelyn: any quick mitigation? revert or change heuristic?

ashwin: proposed immediate mitigation: 1) tighten prefetch threshold (only prefetch for hot prefixes > 3 tokens) 2) prefer int8_probe rather than full fp8_slowpath on single-token batches 3) add a 5ms hysteresis before switching kernels per-request.

sam: will that hurt quality? the fp8 path was added for numeric safety on some models.

ashwin: we measured sample-set BLEU-ish decode diffs on 200 examples: FP8 slowpath reduced hallucination rate by ~0.6% on that set vs int8_probe. but user-visible difference is small. quality delta vs 18% latency regress not worth it for most infra tiers.

marie: I'd prefer a targeted rollback of the kernel-handoff subchange in c3f9b2d and then reintroduce with stronger thresholds. can infra do a canary rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback job started for canary pool 'kv-int8fp8-canary' at 2026-03-18T14:02:40Z.

perf-bot: after rollback baseline run: p50 8.5ms, p99 43ms. memory back to 6.7GB. Regression resolved on canary.

evelyn: sweet. follow-ups:
- add telemetry for 'kernel_switch_count' per request (ashwin)
- add per-prefix calibration smoothing (sam)
- update batching heuristic doc and include small-batch knobs (marie)

ashwin: working on kernel_switch_count now, will push a tiny metric at /metrics.kv.kernel_switch_count with tags {shard, model, prefix_len_bucket}.

sam: I'll prototype a rolling-average smoother for calib_score that biases towards int8 for prefixes < 4 tokens. hoping to keep memory benefits and avoid jitter.

marie: schedule a quick postmortem in eng-runtime tomorrow, add details & perf traces to the ticket. ticket: INF-9242 (I'll add links).

ashwin: screenshot of flame after rollback attached to ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
